claims.statement: Zendesk documents an OAuth refresh token returned with the access token in the authorization code flow and exchanged at /oauth/tokens (grant_type refresh_token) for a new access token and refresh token; the old refresh token stops working immediately, and the default lifetime is 30 days (configurable from 7 to 90 days). The client credentials flow returns no refresh token.

sources.supports: Refresh token: Used behind the scenes to get a new access token when the current one expires. ... Refresh token 30 days by default, configurable from 7 to 90 days ... The old refresh token stops working right away.
Unlike the authorization code flow, no user redirect is required and Zendesk does not return a refresh token.

claims.statement: Zendesk's refresh token tutorial shows the refresh token as a refresh_token member of the JSON response of POST https://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/oauth/tokens (beside access_token, expires_in, token_type, scope and refresh_token_expires_in) and as the refresh_token member of the JSON request body of a refresh request (grant_type refresh_token, with client_id and client_secret, Content-Type application/json).

sources.supports: Zendesk will respond with an access token and a refresh token. (the example response JSON has the members access_token, expires_in, refresh_token, token_type, scope and refresh_token_expires_in)
sources.locator: Exchanging the authorization code for tokens

sources.supports: use your refresh token to request a new access token with the Create Token for Grant Type endpoint: curl https://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/oauth/tokens -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{ "grant_type": "refresh_token", "refresh_token": "{YOUR_REFRESH_TOKEN}", "client_id": "{YOUR_CLIENT_ID}", "client_secret": "{YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET}" }'

claims.statement: Zendesk says that GET /api/v2/oauth/tokens, which inspects tokens, truncates token values including refresh_token for security reasons, and that the refresh token cannot be retrieved by an API after creation.

sources.supports: If you’re using GET /api/v2/oauth/tokens to inspect tokens (rather than create them), token values (including refresh_token) are truncated for security reasons. Securely store the refresh token when it’s first returned (at creation time) as it cannot be retrieved by an API.
sources.locator: Common questions, Why does my refresh token look short

openQuestions.question: The pages show example refresh tokens of differing shapes (32 and 64 characters) and state no format; no shape is recorded.
This candidate is recorded from the claims above only; format, variants, history and benign siblings have not been researched.
The JSON members are documented; the tutorial shows example token values that the page does not state as a format, and none is recorded.
